# NCLEX Prep To-Do List

## 📋 Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1-2)
- [ ] Schedule your NCLEX exam date (gives you a deadline)
- [ ] Take a diagnostic practice test to identify weak areas
- [ ] Choose your main study resource (UWorld, Archer, Kaplan, Mark Klimek, etc.)
- [ ] Create a realistic study schedule (4-6 weeks minimum recommended)
- [ ] Gather supplies: notebook, highlighters, whiteboard, flashcards

## 📚 Phase 2: Content Review (Week 2-4)
- [ ] Review **Safety & Infection Control** (priority area)
- [ ] Study **Pharmacology** (drug classes, suffixes, side effects)
- [ ] Review **Lab Values** (memorize normal ranges)
- [ ] Study **Maternal/Newborn** content
- [ ] Review **Pediatrics** (growth/development, vaccines)
- [ ] Study **Mental Health** (therapeutic communication)
- [ ] Review **Medical-Surgical** by body system
- [ ] Study **Fundamentals** (ADPIE, Maslow's, delegation)
- [ ] Watch Mark Klimek lectures (highly recommended)

## ✏️ Phase 3: Practice Questions (Daily)
- [ ] Complete **75-100 questions per day** minimum
- [ ] Review **EVERY rationale** (right and wrong answers)
- [ ] Keep an error log/notebook of missed concepts
- [ ] Practice **SATA** (Select All That Apply) questions
- [ ] Practice **Next Gen NCLEX (NGN)** case studies
- [ ] Aim for 65%+ consistently on UWorld/Archer

## 🧠 Phase 4: Test-Taking Strategies
- [ ] Learn ABC's (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) prioritization
- [ ] Master Maslow's Hierarchy for priority questions
- [ ] Practice "safety first" thinking
- [ ] Learn therapeutic communication techniques
- [ ] Practice delegation rules (RN vs LPN vs UAP)
- [ ] Eliminate absolute words ("always," "never")

## 🎯 Phase 5: Final Week
- [ ] Take 1-2 full-length practice exams
- [ ] Review error log one final time
- [ ] Light review only - **don't cram**
- [ ] Confirm test location and ID requirements
- [ ] Prepare your test day items (ID, ATT, confirmation)
- [ ] Get 8+ hours of sleep nights before
- [ ] Eat a good breakfast on test day

## 💪 Self-Care (Ongoing)
- [ ] Exercise 3-4x per week
- [ ] Take 1 full day off per week
- [ ] Stay hydrated and eat well
- [ ] Limit social media during study time
- [ ] Join an NCLEX study group/Reddit community
- [ ] Practice positive self-talk

## 🏆 Test Day
- [ ] Arrive 30 minutes early
- [ ] Bring 2 forms of ID
- [ ] Use breaks strategically
- [ ] Read each question carefully
- [ ] Trust your preparation!

**You've got this!** 🎉 Want me to dive deeper into any specific section?
